fm.label: FM radio broadcasting (76-108 MHz: eFM 76-88 for AM stations moved to FM)

notes: USA, Canada, Mexico, Brazil: FM stations only on odd tenths.
USA: 88.1-91.9 MHz reserved for non-commercial radio.
Without a country, the 700 / 800 MHz, 1.8-2 GHz and 3.5 GHz bands get one neutral label: the layouts differ by country.
prompt: 88-108 MHz FM broadcast radio (stations on odd tenths, e.g. 97.1). Cheap FM bugs, wireless mics and car FM transmitters also use it.
108-118 aircraft navigation beacons (VOR, ILS: steady AM carriers, no voice); 118-137 aircraft voice (AM); 137-138 weather satellites.
144-148 2 m amateur radio (APRS 144.39); 148-174 business/public-service radio, marine VHF 156-162.
54-88, 174-216 and 470-608 digital TV; 300-320 car keyfobs, garage remotes, tyre sensors (315).
225-400 military radio; 420-450 70 cm amateur; 433.05-434.79 low-power devices: weather stations, remotes, door/window sensors.
450-470 business radios and walkie-talkies; 698-806 and 824-894 mobile phone bands; 806-824 and 851-869 trunked and public-safety radio.
902-928 ISM: smart meters, LoRa, industrial sensors, some remotes; 1090 aircraft ADS-B.
